CUTOUT.src: LM_PK602 afternoon (FOB plant), 2026-11-19 PM: cutout 68.66, -0.82 from 69.48. Read from the PRIMARY source - the USDA AMS 'National Daily Hog and Pork Summary' whose printed header reads 'Nov 19, 2026 ... Des Moines, Iowa Thu'. Corroborated arithmetically: all SIX primals chain exactly off the independently confirmed 2026-11-18 values - Loin 68.40-2.17=66.23, Butt 97.19-1.22=95.97, Picnic 56.99+0.46=57.45, Rib 127.58+0.82=128.40, Ham 62.90-0.14=62.76, Belly 66.48-1.13=65.35 - and the cutout chains 69.48-0.82=68.66. Total loads 239.20 (pork cuts 208.84 + trim/process 30.36). || 2026-11-23 RUN: still held at 2026-11-19. A 2026-11-20 PM cutout of 67.88 WAS found, described as the lowest since August 2020, in an Ag Optimus COT piece published 2026-11-23 04:25 UTC. It is UNCORROBORATED and was NOT written in: it is a single source, no second rendering of the Nov 20 afternoon report was reachable, and unlike the Nov 19 figure there is no primal set to chain it against. That source was accurate on everything else it could be tested on this session (its Nov 20 Dec and Feb settlements match three other routes to the cent, and two of its lean-hog-index basis figures reconcile exactly), so 67.88 is probably right - but 'probably' is not the standard, and RUNBOOK is explicit that an unverified price is left for the gate to flag. It is recorded HERE, clearly labelled uncorroborated, so a later run can use it as a chain anchor if a second source turns up. The AMS mnreports endpoints were again stale (ams_2498.pdf printed 'October 26, 2026'; lsddhps.pdf 'Oct 23, 2026'), the Barchart S3 mirror was unreachable, no 2026-11-23 PM wire had published by run time, and ThePigSite's latest CME wire is still dated 2026-11-19. Separately, a weekly COMPREHENSIVE cutout of 71.04 dated 2026-11-16 was seen; that is a different series from the daily FOB-plant cutout and is not interchangeable with it. One cross-check worth noting: ThePigSite's 2026-11-18 wire printed the Nov 17 cutout as '66.44' while stating a change of -2.80 from Monday; 71.24-2.80=68.44, the value held here, so that wire has a digit transposition and the 68.44 in this file is confirmed correct.

CARCASS_WT.src: LM_HG201 average carcass weights for the 2026-11-20 slaughter, from the National Daily Direct Prior Day Slaughtered Swine report released 2026-11-23. CONFIRMED by TWO INDEPENDENT RENDERINGS of that report, which agree to the hundredth on every producer purchase type: 220.41 negotiated, 221.42 other market formula, 221.56 swine/pork market formula, 222.54 other purchase arrangement, 221.88 combined producer-sold. The combined figure also reconciles ARITHMETICALLY: head-weighting the four types by the report's own head counts (6,228 / 31,737 / 171,282 / 107,061) gives 221.855 against the printed 221.88, and those head counts plus the 337 withheld negotiated-formula head sum to 316,645, exactly the printed producer-sold total. packer_owned 218.94 required adjudication: the two renderings SWAP the packer-owned and packer-sold labels (218.94 vs 222.89). The 218.94 assignment is used because it is the one that preserves the relationship in this file's own history - packer-owned ran 3.05 lb BELOW combined on 2026-11-17 (215.41 vs 218.46) and 2.94 lb below on 2026-11-20 (218.94 vs 221.88) - whereas 222.89 would put packer-owned above combined, inverting a spread that has been stable. 222.89 is independently accounted for as the packer-sold weight, which also carries the 56.10 packer-sold net. Weights rising into late November is seasonally normal and consistent with wire commentary on heavier weights adding supply. NOTE: the per-type BASE PRICES in this same report did NOT pass verification and were not written - see the NEGOTIATED and PRODUCER_ALL notes.

LH_INDEX.note: 56.32 is the CME Lean Hog Index for 2026-11-18, the latest published as of the 2026-11-20 close (the index runs a two-business-day lag). Single-source on its face - an Ag Optimus COT piece published 2026-11-23 04:25 UTC - but it passes TWO independent arithmetic checks against figures verified here from other sources, which is why it is written in rather than held. The piece states the index stood $3.72 over December: 56.32 - 52.60 (the 2026-11-20 Dec settlement, independently confirmed by four sources) = 3.72 exactly. It states the comparable basis was $2.38 on 2026-11-16: 57.73 (the 2026-11-12 index held here) - 55.35 (the 2026-11-16 Dec close held here) = 2.38 exactly. Both checks reconcile to the cent against values this file already held, and the second also confirms the publication-lag convention. The 2026-11-17 index value was never published to a reachable source, so the series steps from 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18 rather than being padded.
